samples.summary: New `escapeHtml` helper for the CLI consent page has no test with hostile input
samples.evidence: `escapeHtml` (auth.controller.ts:32-39) is added specifically to make attacker-influenceable values (`nonce`, `codeChallenge`, `port`) safe to interpolate into the consent HTML. The only tests that touch it are in auth.controller.spec.ts's `GET /auth/github — CLI consent page` block, whose fixture uses benign values (`nonce: 'n0nce-x/y'`, `codeChallenge: 'c'.repeat(43)`, `port: 9876`). No test feeds a value containing `"`, `<`, `>` or `'` and asserts it comes back entity-escaped, so removing any of the five `.replace()` calls (or the `escapeHtml(href)` call entirely) leaves the whole suite green. Note the guard only length-bounds `nonce` (no character pattern), so quotes can reach this template. The `continueLink` helper in the spec merely *un*escapes the href to parse a URL — it asserts nothing about escaping.

samples.summary: New `?error=` banner on the login form has no frontend test
samples.evidence: `LoginForm` now reads `useSearchParams()` and renders an alert from `ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR` — new user-visible behavior that is the only feedback a user gets from the backend's `login?error=login_state` redirect. Grepping the frontend for `login_state` / `LoginForm` finds only `login-form.tsx` and `app/login/page.tsx`; there is no `login-form.test.tsx` (the only component test in `src/components/__tests__` is `datasource-dialog.test.tsx`). The frontend vitest lane runs, so a test was possible; both branches (known key vs fallback, and the no-error case rendering nothing) are unasserted.

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`: the TTY branch and the 0600 file mode are never asserted
samples.evidence: `announceLoginUrl` has two branches. login-callback.test.ts only exercises the non-TTY branch (vitest stderr is not a TTY): it asserts the path is mentioned and the file content equals the URL. Nothing tests (a) `process.stderr.isTTY === true` printing the URL to stderr and writing no file, (b) the third branch's message when the write fails, or (c) the `mode: 0o600` / `rmSync`-before-write behaviour the comment sells as the security property ("readable only by you"). Grep for `0o600` in packages/cli/test matches only session.test.ts, not the login URL file.

samples.summary: The `sawUnboundCode` timeout message branch is untested
samples.evidence: `startCallbackServer` now distinguishes two timeout errors: the plain 'Login timed out.' and a longer 'callback carried no `state`… server may predate the CLI loopback binding' message when a code arrived with `state === null`. The timeout test in login-callback.test.ts (`waits out the server’s whole five-minute login window`) only asserts `rejects.toThrow(/timed out/i)` on a server that received no callback at all, so the `sawUnboundCode` branch — and the flag being set only for `state === null` rather than for a wrong state — is never exercised.

`codeForStatus` maps 401/403 → UNAUTHORIZED, >=500 → SYSTEM, everything else → HTTP_ERROR, and `failFromBackend` exits 1 only for HTTP_ERROR. login-callback.test.ts covers exactly the 401 case (exit 2) and the 502 case (exit 2). No test drives a 4xx that is not 401/403 (e.g. 400 or 404), so the HTTP_ERROR code and the exit-1 path — the only branch distinguishing exit 1 from exit 2 — never runs.

samples.summary: The `command: commandPath(this)` wiring into the import/upload/download orchestrators is asserted nowhere
samples.evidence: docs.ts, files.ts, notes.ts and slides.ts now pass `command: commandPath(this)` into `runDocsImport`/`runFilesUpload`/`runFilesDownload`/`runNotesImport`/`runSlidesImport`, and those functions stamp it into every envelope. The orchestrator unit tests (docs-import.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts, slides-import.test.ts, files-upload.test.ts, files-download.test.ts) never pass `command` — grep for `command` in docs-import.test.ts returns nothing — so they only exercise the omitted-command shape. output.test.ts covers `errorEnvelope`/`backendErrorEnvelope` in isolation and covers attribution only for `outputError` call sites. Dropping the `command:` argument at any of these five call sites would leave the whole suite green.

samples.summary: CLI callback tests bypass the guard, so the guard→controller handshake (cookie names, consent gate) is never exercised together
samples.evidence: `startCliLogin` calls `cliAuthStore.createState({...})` directly and hand-builds `cookies: { wafflebase_cli_state: … }`, rather than running `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` to mint the state and cookie. The controller reads the cookie via `loginCookieName(configService, CLI_STATE_COOKIE)` while the guard writes it via the same helper — but no test proves the two agree on any deployment where the name is `__Host-`-prefixed (both spec files pin the bare-name case only, and the controller spec's ConfigService returns undefined for GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL). A prefix mismatch between issue and read would refuse every real login with both suites green.

`issueLoginCookie` throws `InternalServerErrorException('Cannot start a login session')` when the response object cannot set cookies — added deliberately so a mis-wired response fails visibly instead of producing unbindable logins. github-auth.guard.spec.ts's `contextFor` always supplies a `cookie` function, and no test builds a context whose response lacks it, so the branch never executes.

samples.summary: Controller-side CLI port range check and `loginErrorUrl` trailing-slash normalisation are untested
samples.evidence: The callback re-checks `port < 1024 || port > 65535` and throws BadRequestException; no test in auth.controller.spec.ts constructs a stored CLI state with an out-of-range port (the guard now rejects those, so this branch is only reachable via a state minted another way — exactly what a test could pin). Likewise `loginErrorUrl` strips a trailing slash from FRONTEND_URL, but the spec's ConfigService returns 'http://localhost:5173' without one, so the `.replace(/\/$/, '')` is never exercised.

samples.summary: The wiring of `logSafeUrl` into the pino request serializer is untested
samples.evidence: `logSafeUrl` itself is thoroughly covered by log-safe-url.spec.ts, but nothing asserts it is actually applied in app.module.ts's `serializers.req`. Reverting that one line to `url: req.url` would silently restore full query-string logging with every test green. No spec file exists for app.module (glob over packages/backend/src/*.spec.ts).

finding.summary: New `escapeHtml` helper for the CLI consent page has no test with hostile input
finding.evidence: `escapeHtml` (auth.controller.ts:32-39) is added specifically to make attacker-influenceable values (`nonce`, `codeChallenge`, `port`) safe to interpolate into the consent HTML. The only tests that touch it are in auth.controller.spec.ts's `GET /auth/github — CLI consent page` block, whose fixture uses benign values (`nonce: 'n0nce-x/y'`, `codeChallenge: 'c'.repeat(43)`, `port: 9876`). No test feeds a value containing `"`, `<`, `>` or `'` and asserts it comes back entity-escaped, so removing any of the five `.replace()` calls (or the `escapeHtml(href)` call entirely) leaves the whole suite green. Note the guard only length-bounds `nonce` (no character pattern), so quotes can reach this template. The `continueLink` helper in the spec merely *un*escapes the href to parse a URL — it asserts nothing about escaping.

verdict.reason: The finding's testable core — that no assertion exercises `escapeHtml`, so "removing any of the five .replace() calls (or the escapeHtml(href) call entirely) leaves the whole suite green" — is false. auth.controller.spec.ts:581 asserts `expect(html).toContain('/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876')`, i.e. the entity-escaped `&` separator in the rendered Continue link. Removing `.replace(/&/g,'&')` from escapeHtml (auth.controller.ts:41) or dropping `escapeHtml(...)` at auth.controller.ts:172 makes the HTML contain a raw `&` and that assertion fails. Furthermore, `&` is the only character that can actually reach the template unescaped: `href` is assembled from `new URLSearchParams(...).toString()` (auth.controller.ts:165-171), whose form-urlencoded serializer percent-encodes `"`, `'`, `<`, `>` before escapeHtml sees them, and the other escaped value is `String(consent.port)` where port is a number (`Number(port)` in github-auth.guard.ts ~314). So the escaping behavior that is observable at this call site is covered by a real, failing-on-regression assertion; the demanded `"`/`<` assertion could not be written against this template anyway. Not a fake-coverage or missing-coverage defect under the test-adequacy rubric.
